note: Every entry MUST carry source and status. See README.md - statutory, standard, observed and derived entries may influence decisions; hypothesis entries are stored to be verified or refuted, never acted upon. A 'derived' entry is reasoned domain knowledge: it must state its reasoning and may never carry a number - shares, percentages and effect sizes require measurement, not argument. detectionKeywords are the words a plan would realistically contain if it covers that capability, used by the compliance gate to test coverage by evidence. appliesWhenKeywords are the words that show a conditional duty's condition actually holds - without them a game that sells nothing gets told about loot-box odds.

capabilities.title: Accessible interface
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product has any browser or app interface
jobs: When I cannot use a mouse, I want to complete every task with a keyboard, so that the product is usable at all
When I have low vision, I want text I can actually read, so that I can use the product without assistance

expectations.requirement: WCAG 2.1 level AA: keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, 4.5:1 text contrast
expectations.source: European Accessibility Act (Directive 2019/882), applicable from 2025-06-28; harmonised standard EN 301 549 which adopts WCAG 2.1 AA; in the US enforced under ADA Title III case law
expectations.note: A property of every screen. Delivered as criteria inside each UI slice - never as one separate 'make it accessible' epic, which is how accessibility reliably fails to happen.

capabilities.title: Data subject rights
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product stores personal data of identifiable people
jobs: When I ask what you hold about me, I want to receive it, so that I can verify it
When I ask you to erase my data, I want it actually erased, so that I keep control of it

expectations.requirement: Export of a data subject's own data on request, and erasure on request, within the statutory deadline
expectations.source: GDPR (Regulation 2016/679) Art. 15 (right of access) and Art. 17 (right to erasure); one month response deadline under Art. 12(3)

capabilities.title: Lawful basis and consent
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product collects personal data or loads third-party tracking or analytics
jobs: When I arrive, I want to decide what is collected about me before it happens, so that the choice is genuinely mine

expectations.requirement: Opt-in consent captured before any non-essential cookie or tracker loads; refusing must be as easy as accepting; the choice is recorded and revocable
expectations.source: GDPR Art. 6 and Art. 7 (conditions for consent); ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) on storing or accessing information on terminal equipment

expectations.requirement: Use an established consent platform rather than a hand-rolled banner
expectations.source: Derived from domain reasoning, 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
expectations.reasoning: Consent rules change by jurisdiction and over time, and a hand-rolled banner freezes one reading of them into the product. The reasoning is about maintenance burden, not about measured compliance rates.

capabilities.title: Backup with verified restore
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product holds data whose loss would harm the client's business
jobs: When something destroys our data, I want it back, so that the business survives the incident

expectations.requirement: Regular backups AND a restore that has actually been performed and verified, not merely configured
expectations.source: GDPR Art. 32(1)(c) requires the ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner following an incident
expectations.note: An untested backup does not satisfy the requirement, so acceptance criteria must include a real restore.

capabilities.title: Account recovery
jobs: When I am locked out, I want a way back in, so that I do not lose access to my own business data

expectations.requirement: A self-service recovery path for a locked-out account, including the owner account
expectations.source: Derived from domain reasoning, 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
expectations.reasoning: Credentials are lost routinely - people leave, phones break, passwords are forgotten. Without a way back in, the owner is locked out of their own business data and the only remedy is the vendor, which is not a product but a dependency. Nothing here claims how often it happens; only that the path must exist.

capabilities.title: Legally required site disclosures (Germany)
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product is a commercial site or service operated for the German market
jobs: When I look at who I am buying from, I want to see who they legally are, so that I know who I am dealing with

expectations.requirement: Imprint (Impressum) reachable from every page: legal entity, address, contact, register number and VAT ID where applicable
expectations.source: §5 Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz (DDG, successor to §5 TMG)
expectations.note: Germany-specific enforcement reality: a missing or incomplete Impressum is a standard Abmahnung target - a paid cease-and-desist letter from competitors or law firms. The cost lands on the client, not on us, which is exactly why it cannot be left to the brief to mention.

expectations.requirement: Withdrawal rights: 14-day right of withdrawal with the statutory instruction text and a model withdrawal form, for consumer sales
expectations.source: Directive 2011/83/EU on consumer rights, transposed in BGB §§312g, 355 and Art. 246a EGBGB

expectations.requirement: Prices shown inclusive of VAT, with shipping costs stated and total shown before the order is binding; the order button must be labelled unambiguously (Button-Lösung)
expectations.source: Preisangabenverordnung (PAngV); BGB §312j(3) requiring an order button labelled e.g. 'zahlungspflichtig bestellen'

expectations.requirement: Consent for non-essential cookies and trackers under the German transposition, not only the GDPR baseline
expectations.source: §25 TDDDG (formerly TTDSG), transposing ePrivacy Art. 5(3)

capabilities.title: State privacy rights and sales tax (United States)
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product serves customers in the United States
jobs: When I want out of having my data sold, I want a clear way to say so, so that my choice is respected
When I buy, I want to be charged the right tax, so that neither of us has a problem later

expectations.requirement: Consumer privacy rights - access, deletion, and opt-out of sale/sharing - for residents of states that grant them
expectations.source: CCPA as amended by CPRA (California); comparable acts in Virginia (VCDPA), Colorado (CPA), Connecticut (CTDPA), Utah (UCPA) and further states
expectations.note: Unlike the EU there is no single federal regime; applicability depends on state and on business thresholds. Treated here as required by default because the cost of wrongly omitting it exceeds the cost of building it.

expectations.requirement: Sales tax calculated per destination jurisdiction, via an established tax service rather than hand-maintained rates
expectations.source: South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018) established economic nexus; roughly 11,000 taxing jurisdictions exist, so rates cannot be maintained by hand
expectations.note: Architectural, not cosmetic: retrofitting destination-based tax means rewriting order totals, so it belongs in the first decomposition.

capabilities.title: Locally expected payment methods
jobs: When I pay, I want to use the method I always use, so that I do not abandon the purchase

expectations.requirement: Germany: offer SEPA direct debit, PayPal, and purchase-on-invoice alongside cards; card-only checkout underperforms in this market
expectations.source: Derived from domain reasoning, 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
expectations.reasoning: Payment habits are country-specific and a checkout that cannot accept how someone normally pays ends the transaction at its last step - the most expensive place to lose it. That invoice and direct debit are long-established consumer payment methods in Germany is documentary fact, not a measurement. The original wording claimed underperformance without a number behind it; the requirement now stands on the structural point, and any share remains unmeasured.

expectations.requirement: Strong customer authentication on electronic payments in the EU
expectations.source: PSD2 (Directive 2015/2366) Art. 97 and Commission Delegated Regulation 2018/389 on strong customer authentication

capabilities.title: An enquiry is visibly received
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product lets someone send an enquiry, request or message that a human is meant to answer
jobs: When I send an enquiry, I want to know it arrived, so that I am not left guessing whether to try somewhere else

expectations.requirement: Automatic acknowledgement to the sender the moment an enquiry is submitted, stating what was received and what happens next
expectations.source: Matelso Lead Management Study 2024 (100 companies in construction, mechanical engineering, IT, automotive), read 2026-08-15 via ldb.de: only 4 automatic acknowledgements were received across 91 enquiries. See observations/site-enquiry-response-2026-08-15.json, including the fact that the study's publisher sells lead-management software.
expectations.note: Chosen because it is the one figure in that study that a product can actually act on. Everything else it measured - whether a human eventually replied, whether the phone was picked up - no website can guarantee. Silence after sending is indistinguishable from not being heard, and this is both the cheapest link in the chain and the one almost nobody builds.

capabilities.title: What a booking product is expected to contain
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product books appointments, resources or time slots
jobs: When I have booked, I want to be reminded, so that I do not simply forget and lose the slot
When I cannot come, I want to say so without phoning, so that I am not counted as a no-show

expectations.requirement: Automatic reminder to the customer before the appointment, by email or SMS
expectations.source: Survey of 4 real German booking products for small service businesses, 2026-08-15 (cituro, eTermin, SuperSaaS, Terminbuch.de) - claimed by 4 of 4. See observations/booking-DE-2026-08-15.json for the method and its limits.
expectations.note: Table stakes in the market and almost never present in a client brief - exactly the shape of gap this corpus exists to fill. The survey measures what vendors ADVERTISE, not what products contain, so it is evidence of market expectation.

expectations.requirement: A way to handle a slot that frees up - a waiting list, or filling the gap when someone cancels
expectations.source: Same survey, 2026-08-15 - claimed by 4 of 4, either as an explicit waiting list or as reminders sold specifically as no-show reduction.
expectations.note: An empty chair is the loss this entire product class is sold against.

expectations.requirement: The customer can cancel or move the appointment themselves, without contacting the business
expectations.source: Derived from domain reasoning, 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
expectations.note: Deliberately left inert despite looking obviously right. The market does not treat it as a selling point, which is precisely why no brief will ask for it - but wanting it to be true is not evidence that it is.
expectations.reasoning: A reminder tells the business that someone intends to come; it does not free the slot when they cannot. Only the customer can know they will not make it, and only in time to matter if they can act without waiting for opening hours. Without this the booking degrades into a no-show, which is the exact loss the product is bought to prevent. No effect size is claimed.

capabilities.title: Youth protection and age rating
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product is a game, or any product whose audience plausibly includes minors
jobs: When my child uses this, I want to decide what they are exposed to and what they can spend, so that I stay the parent
When I publish a game in Germany, I want a valid age label, so that the platform may legally distribute it

expectations.requirement: A valid age label (USK) shown clearly, including for purely digital and online distribution - not only physical media
expectations.source: §14a Jugendschutzgesetz (JuSchG) as amended by the 2021 reform, which extended the age-labelling duty to online game platforms
expectations.note: Blocking, not cosmetic: without a label the game cannot be legally distributed on German platforms at all. Belongs in the first decomposition because the rating depends on mechanics that are decided early.

expectations.requirement: Structural precautions for online games: means to limit spending, disclosure of game mechanics and of the probabilities behind randomised rewards, restrictions on advertising aimed at minors, and usage-limiting options
expectations.source: §24a JuSchG (Vorsorgemaßnahmen) as amended 2021
expectations.note: The 2021 reform makes loot boxes, chat and excessive-use mechanics into rating factors: the USK reports that roughly 30% of tested games with online functions received a HIGHER age rating because of such usage risks. So these mechanics do not merely add legal duties - they narrow the game's legal audience, which is a commercial decision disguised as a design one and must be surfaced during decomposition, not after.

expectations.requirement: Verifiable parental consent before collecting personal data from children under 13, with age screening that does not invite misreporting
expectations.source: COPPA Rule, 16 CFR Part 312; FTC amendments finalised January 2025 with a compliance deadline of 2026-04-22, which expanded disclosure duties, tightened verifiable-consent standards and added biometric identifiers (fingerprint, voiceprint, iris, genetic data) to covered personal information
expectations.note: Enforcement is real and expensive: the FTC's Epic Games settlement totalled $520M, of which $275M was the COPPA penalty. In FTC v. Cognosphere (Genshin Impact) the operator was held to be a child-directed service and required to obtain parental consent for under-16 loot box purchases. A game does not have to be aimed at children to be found child-directed.

expectations.requirement: Age assurance may collect data for the sole purpose of establishing age
expectations.source: FTC policy statement, February 2026: the Commission will not bring a COPPA Rule enforcement action against operators collecting, using and disclosing personal information solely to determine a user's age via age verification technologies
expectations.note: Recorded because it removes the usual objection that age checking is itself a privacy violation - it is a safe harbour, so 'we cannot check age without breaking privacy law' is not a valid reason to omit age screening.

capabilities.title: Honest purchase flows and randomised rewards
capabilities.appliesWhen: the product sells anything inside itself, especially randomised or virtual-currency purchases
jobs: When I spend money, I want to have meant to spend it, so that I am not charged by accident
When I buy a chance at something, I want to know the actual odds, so that I am not deceived about what I am buying

expectations.requirement: Disclose the real probabilities and the real cost of randomised rewards, in the currency the player actually paid
expectations.source: FTC Act §5 as applied in FTC v. Cognosphere (Genshin Impact), which charged misrepresentation of loot box odds and required clear disclosure of odds and costs; in Germany the same disclosure is required as a Vorsorgemaßnahme under §24a JuSchG
expectations.note: Virtual-currency layers are treated as part of the deception when they obscure real cost, so a plan that prices items only in a made-up currency has not satisfied this.

expectations.requirement: Disclose the odds of each outcome of a randomised virtual item before purchase, as a condition of being distributed at all on the mobile stores
expectations.source: Apple App Store Review Guidelines §3.1.1, which requires apps offering loot boxes or other randomised virtual items to disclose the odds of each item type prior to purchase; Google Play carries an equivalent disclosure requirement
expectations.note: A second, independent source for the same duty, and the one that bites first. Store review blocks the release outright, months before any regulator would look - so on mobile this is not a legal risk to weigh but a shipping gate. Recorded as standard rather than statutory because it is platform policy, not law; it is nonetheless mandatory in practice for anything distributed through those stores.

expectations.requirement: No dark patterns in purchase flows: purchase confirmation must be deliberate, and controls must not be placed or timed so that an ordinary action triggers a charge
expectations.source: FTC Act §5 as applied in FTC v. Epic Games (2023): $245M in refunds for dark patterns, where players were charged while the game woke from sleep, during loading screens, or by pressing a button adjacent to the purchase control, with button layouts differing between platforms
expectations.note: The specific findings are recorded because they are concrete and testable design rules, not a vague call to be fair: no charge without a deliberate confirmation, no purchase control adjacent to a common non-purchase control, no purchase reachable from an inactive or loading state, consistent layout across platforms.

capabilities.detectionKeywordsNote: These say the DUTY is addressed, not that the topic exists. They previously included 'loot box', 'in-app purchase' and 'virtual currency' - which are the words that show the duty APPLIES. A plan describing purchases therefore scored as having disclosed their odds simply by mentioning purchases, so the one duty most worth catching was silently never reported. Condition words belong in appliesWhenKeywords; coverage words belong here.

capabilities.title: Outcome measurement
jobs: When the product has been running for a month, I want to know whether it is doing what I bought it for, so that I can decide what to change

expectations.requirement: Metrics derived from the client's stated outcome via Goal-Question-Metric: the goal, the questions that would reveal whether it is being met, and only the metrics answering those questions
expectations.source: Method: Basili & Weiss, 'A Methodology for Collecting Valid Software Engineering Data', IEEE TSE 1984; GQM as used in the NASA Software Engineering Laboratory. The requirement that every product carry it is derived - operator decision 2026-08-14.
expectations.note: The method is cited; the claim that every product needs it is this system's own position, adopted by operator decision 2026-08-14.
expectations.reasoning: A product that ships without a way to tell whether it did what it was bought for cannot be improved, argued about, or defended - every later decision about it becomes taste. The method is Goal-Question-Metric so that the metrics follow from the client's own stated outcome instead of being whatever was easy to count. Operator decision, 2026-08-14: every delivered product carries this. No effect size is claimed.
